opportunities.title: Neighborhood Library Solar Resilience Hubs
opportunities.summary: Install rooftop solar and battery storage systems at county libraries to serve as neighborhood cooling centers and emergency shelters.
opportunities.rationale: Harris County faces Very High ratings for heat waves and inland flooding, enduring 66 hot days a year and 13 major disaster declarations.
plan: Audit electrical infrastructure and structural roof integrity at candidate library locations.
Design solar arrays with battery energy storage sized for critical emergency loads.
Issue a competitive solicitation to procure qualified clean energy design-build contractors.
Secure necessary building permits and grid interconnection approvals from local utility CenterPoint Energy.
Install and commission the rooftop solar panels and battery storage backup systems.
Establish community emergency operational protocols designating facilities as heat shelters.
first_steps: Audit electrical infrastructure and structural roof integrity at candidate library locations.
Design solar arrays with battery energy storage sized for critical emergency loads.

Install and commission the rooftop solar panels and battery storage backup systems.
Establish community emergency operational protocols designating facilities as heat shelters.
compliance: Confirm municipal facility use and emergency shelter designations with Houston Library Board.
Verify electric interconnection requirements with local transmission utility CenterPoint Energy.
Check building code compliance for emergency backup power and commercial electrical storage.

need_fits.text: Provides backup power, cooling, and shelter to safeguard vulnerable residents during extreme heat waves and inland flooding emergencies.

course_of_action: Conduct structural engineering evaluation of the Moody Neighborhood Library roof.
Install commercial solar array and battery storage system on facility grounds.
Commission emergency backup power circuits for community cooling and charging.
compliance: Submit interconnection study request to CenterPoint Energy.
Obtain municipal electrical and building permits from City of Houston.

course_of_action: Perform structural and electrical assessment of Shepard-Acres Homes Neighborhood Library.
Deploy solar photovoltaic panels and integrated storage to back up critical systems.
Establish facility protocol for severe weather shelter and cooling response.
compliance: Submit utility interconnection package to CenterPoint Energy.
Verify municipal zoning and public facility safety standards.

Commission facilities into commercial service to provide firm, clean capacity.

opportunities.title: Local Dam Small Hydropower Retrofit
opportunities.summary: Install low-head hydropower turbine generation at Lake Houston Dam to produce continuous, emissions-free electricity from existing water discharges.
opportunities.rationale: Lake Houston Dam is a locally owned non-powered structure with 4.9 MW of modelled hydropower potential, leveraging skilled local construction trades.
plan: Execute a detailed engineering and flow feasibility study on Lake Houston Dam discharge structures.
Formulate a development agreement with the local municipal dam operating authority.
Submit regulatory filings to federal and state hydro and water licensing bodies.
Procure hydroelectric turbine equipment and design-build civil engineering contractors.
Construct intake retrofits, powerhouse facilities, and local electrical interconnection lines.
Commission 4.9 MW hydro generator to inject baseline clean power into the grid.

narrative.summary: Harris County faces severe natural hazard risks from heat waves and flooding, high rates of impaired surface waters, elevated air pollution, and dozens of non-compliant drinking water systems. To address these challenges, the county can leverage its public facilities, extensive brownfields, non-powered dams, and industrial footprint. Key opportunities include establishing solar resilience hubs at libraries, restoring impaired stream corridors, deploying community solar on vacant brownfield parcels, adding small hydropower to a county-managed dam, assisting violated drinking water systems, and developing clean storage at retiring fossil plant sites.
caveats: The opportunities were written by Gemini from the needs, factors and sites in this report. Each was checked to use only this report's needs, sites and numbers. Feasibility and cost were not checked. Course-of-action and compliance lines are planning checks, not legal advice; confirm permits and local rules with counsel and the right agencies.
Figures marked as estimates are rough. The assumptions behind each one are listed with it.
A listed funding program is a lead to check, not a finding that the county or project is eligible. Confirm status and deadlines with the agency.
Electricity bill and grid carbon figures are state averages, not county figures.
